kicker: Sentences break into little stones; AI reads, remembers and charges by the stone.

shatter.label: Sentences into stones
shatter.stonesAria: Token stones. Left and right arrows choose a stone; Enter tosses it up.
shatter.live: The sentence was split into {n} tokens: {list}.
shatter.insight: AI doesn’t read like we do: sentences are cut into tokens — small pieces of text — then turned into numbers.

detail.text: In English, one token is about 4 characters on average — roughly ¾ of a word.

compare.label: Vietnamese and English
compare.breakAria: Split both sentences into tokens to compare
pairs: Son này giữ màu suốt tám tiếng.
Cảm ơn bạn đã đặt hàng.

insight.text: The same idea in Vietnamese is often cut into more tokens than in English: it takes a bit more room and costs a bit more.

detail.text: This tokenizer is only a simulation; every model splits text its own way, so real numbers will differ.

bowl.label: The context bowl

messages.text: Hi Lan, nice to meet you!
Write a caption for my new lipstick.

bowl.name: Lan
bowl.forgot: Sorry, I can no longer see your name.
bowl.liveOut: The {n} oldest tokens fell out of the bowl.
bowl.art: A stone bowl holding the conversation’s token stones.

windowFact.text: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, Sep 3, 2026) takes about 1 million tokens of context.

bowl.insight: The context window is AI’s “working memory”: when it’s full, the oldest part falls out and AI can’t see it anymore.

detail.text: It depends on the app: some cut off the beginning, others summarize it. Good habit: when a chat runs long, sum up the key points and start a new one.

scale.label: The token scale
scale.question: Write 2 captions for a new lipstick.
scale.reply: Red lips, confident all day. Bold red, big bright smile!
scale.art: A balance scale: the left pan holds the tokens you send in, the right pan holds the tokens AI writes out, with a stack of bill coins beside it.

tilt.even: The two pans are nearly balanced.

insight.text: Tokens are how AI is billed: both the text you send in and the text AI writes out count.

detail.text: With many services, tokens AI writes out cost more than tokens you send in. Good habit: ask briefly and paste only the parts you need.

quiz.q: In a very long chat, why might AI “forget” what you said first?
options: It went past the context window
AI is ignoring you on purpose
AI ran out of battery midway
quiz.explain: The context window only holds a set number of tokens; when it’s full, the oldest part can fall out.

summary: AI reads text as tokens — both memory and cost are counted in tokens.
